standards.name: FAANG sample metadata specification
standards.abstract: This specification describes metadata for biological samples collected in FAANG projects: donor animals, tissue specimens, primary cells, cell cultures, pools of specimens, and related biological materials. Metadata are expected to be registered in EMBL-EBI BioSamples and include identifiers, descriptive text, ontology-backed types, dates, numeric measurements with units, and links to protocols or related records. The document is published and maintained by the FAANG Data Coordination Centre (FAANG DCC) as part of their data and archival guidance; it defines required, recommended and optional attributes for different material types and indicates acceptable data types (e.g., text, ontology term, date, URL) and controlled vocabularies/ontologies to use.

classification.rationale: The source is organized as a metadata specification listing named attributes with explicit data types and, in many cases, enumerated allowed values or precise unit constraints (e.g. "Sample name (text)", "Material (ontology term)", "birth date(date)YYYY-MM-DD"). This is genuine field-level structure (a metadata table), not prose guidance or a staged workflow.

standards.name: FAANG experiment metadata specification
standards.abstract: This specification covers metadata for molecular biology experiments performed on biological specimens (organisms, cells, cell cultures) where the data modality is primarily sequencing experiments (archived in SRA/ENA/NCBI/DDBJ) or array experiments (ArrayExpress/GEO). The document, maintained by the FAANG metadata working group and hosted in the FAANG GitHub repository and related wiki pages, defines required, recommended and optional attributes for experiment records and provides assay-specific attribute sets (e.g. ATAC-seq, Bisulfite sequencing, ChIP-seq, DNase-seq, Hi-C, RNA-seq). It addresses the problem of consistent experiment-level metadata for archival and sharing, specifying attribute names, data types and controlled lists where relevant.

classification.rationale: The source material lists explicit attribute names paired with specific data types and, in many cases, enumerated allowed values. It is presented as a concrete metadata table/checklist (attribute name (data type) description) rather than prose guidance or a sequence of steps.

sample.descr: BioSamples identifier for the specimen used in the experiment

standards.name: FAANG analysis metadata specification
standards.abstract: This specification defines metadata to describe computational analyses performed on raw experimental data (for example, sequencing reads from ChIP-seq experiments that are aligned, QCed, and used for peak calling). The document is maintained in the FAANG (Functional Annotation of Animal Genomes) metadata repository and is intended to capture for each analysis the input files, reference data (e.g. genome assembly, gene set), the analysis protocol (software, versions, full command lines, containers/VMs), quality-control metrics and file-naming conventions to ensure reproducibility and unambiguous archival. The specification is a DCC-maintained guidance document in the FAANG repository and is aimed at standardizing metadata for archived analysis results so they can be reproduced and interpreted.

classification.rationale: The source is a metadata specification that lists named attributes and, in several cases, gives explicit data types (e.g. “total reads (number)”), and prescribes concrete field-like items (input data, reference data, analysis protocol and its subcomponents, QC attributes, and filename components). This is a field-level metadata schema rather than purely prose guidance, so it is best represented as a MetadataTable.

standards.name: FAANG data type definitions
standards.abstract: This document defines the allowed data types and expected formats for attributes used in FAANG sample submissions to the BioSamples system. It covers common attribute modalities such as dates, numeric values with units, ontology references (e.g. NCBI Taxonomy or UBERON), URLs (including protocol links), free text, and composite location attributes (name, latitude, longitude). The guidance is maintained by the FAANG data coordination centre (FAANG DCC) and is intended to ensure consistent reporting of attribute values (including use of term sources and IDs) when submitting sample records to BioSamples.

classification.rationale: The source presents a list of named data-types (each with a concrete expected format and submission requirements) rather than prose instructions. Each entry names a field/data type and specifies its concrete format (e.g. ISO 8601 for dates, NCBI Taxonomy ID for species, numeric values with units, composite location fields), matching the definition of a metadata table of field types.

date.name: date
date.descr: Dates in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD for dates or YYYY-MM for months); format must be reported as the 'units'.
date.evidence: Dates should be reported in an [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format,  YYYY-MM-DD for dates or YYYY-MM for months. To ensure clarity, the format must be reported as the 'units'.

ontology term.name: ontology term
ontology term.descr: Reference to an ontology term: attribute value should be the term label, term source the ontology, and term source ID the ontology identifier; use exact term labels where direct links are not supported.
ontology term.evidence: A reference to an ontology term. The attribute value should be the term label. The term source should be the ontology used, and the term source ID should be an ID from that ontology. For example, cerebral cortex could be  described with an ontology term from 'UBERON' with ontology ID of 'UBERON:0000956' and the attribute value is 'cerebral cortex'. Though in the experiment submission, direct links to ontologies cannot be submitted as attributes. The use of ontology terms is still encouraged by setting the attribute value to exactly match the term name in the ontology.

standards.name: FAANG JSON Schema validation rulesets
standards.abstract: These files are JSON Schema validation rules used to validate experiment metadata submitted to the FAANG (Functional Annotation of Animal Genomes) project. They describe required and optional metadata about experiments and samples (assay type, storage, processing, protocols, project membership, timing intervals, etc.), where metadata values are represented as JSON objects, strings, enums and URIs. The rulesets are maintained in the FAANG metadata GitHub repository and are designed for use with the FAANG metadata validation library (https://github.com/FAANG/validate-metadata). They include both current validation rules and legacy (less strict) variants for pre-existing projects that cannot meet the full FAANG standard.

classification.rationale: The source material is a set of JSON Schema files that present a concrete, field-level metadata structure: each top-level property is named and given an explicit JSON type, constraints (required, enum, pattern, format), and descriptions. This is genuine field-level metadata (a MetadataTable), not prose guidance or a procedural DAG.
